title: Accelerating Mixture of Experts Training With Rail Optimized InfiniBand Networking in Crusoe Cloud
talk_summary: A Crusoe Cloud product manager describes rail-optimized InfiniBand cluster networking for distributed MoE training, including NVIDIA SHARP/PXN in-network switching to cut cross-rail hops. They report synthetic NCCL gains and a 14% end-to-end training speedup on a 240x H100 Mixtral fine-tune.

takeaways.technique: Separate high-bandwidth backend fabric from front-end traffic
takeaways.what_they_do: They isolate GPU-to-GPU traffic on a dedicated low-latency fabric, keeping general internet/VPC traffic on a separate front-end network so bulk inter-node communication isn't contending with normal traffic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all the communication between the gpus is happening on the Standalone separate Network that is uh really high performance low latency

takeaways.what_they_do: They start network exchange while computation is still running to hide transfer latency behind useful work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the computation and communication overlap allows you to start the network exchange or the data data exchange when the computation is still ongoing
takeaways.numbers: reduced network share of training time by ~10%, leaving ~25% still on network

takeaways.technique: Measure end-to-end metric, not synthetic benchmark
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly discount synthetic NCCL numbers and validate against real time-to-train on the actual workload (MoE fine-tune).
takeaways.evidence_quote: those numbers are synthetic and more are showing you the workload that is applied to your network what customers care about is the time to train
takeaways.numbers: 50% small-message / 50% large-message synthetic gains vs 14% real end-to-end improvement
